 By BVM Sportsdesk, 11/11/2026 Main Story: The 2026-27 ONE Flyweight Muay Thai World Grand Prix opens Nov. 13 at Bangkok’s Lumpinee Stadium, with Rodtang Jitmuangnon facing Nong-O Hama and rising contenders Shimon Yoshinari and Ramadan Ondash meeting in the co-main event. The eight-fighter tournament offers a path to the Grand Prix belt and ONE world title, with the opening bouts testing whether established stars or emerging talent are best positioned to claim them.
 By the Numbers 8 fighters in the Grand Prix; the winner earns the silver Grand Prix belt and ONE Flyweight Muay Thai World Title.
 Two quarterfinals feature four of the division’s top-five ranked contenders.
 Shimon is 22 with a 27-1 record; Ondash is 20.
 Contenders are pursuing US$100,000 contracts.
 Yes, But Rodtang brings proven pressure and power, but returns to Muay Thai after competing under kickboxing rules and suffering a fifth-round TKO loss in his April 2026 rematch with Takeru Segawa. Nong-O, a former champion with deep experience, is coming off a knockout loss in his bid for the vacant flyweight title. Shimon and Ondash, meanwhile, arrive with momentum but must prove themselves against the division’s top names.
 State of Play Rodtang vs. Nong-O headlines the quarterfinals after their originally scheduled title fight was canceled.
 Shimon and Ondash meet in the co-main event; the winner advances to face the winner of the legends’ bout.
 The event streams exclusively for members at live.onefc.com from Lumpinee Stadium in Bangkok.
 What’s Next The Nov. 13 quarterfinal winners move closer to the tournament title and a shot at the ONE flyweight crown. The results will also reveal whether the veterans can hold off a fast-rising generation—or whether the young contenders can reshape the bracket.
 Bottom Line This opening night puts legacies and a new generation’s ambitions on the same path to a world title: the legends must prove they still belong, while Shimon and Ondash have a chance to show the future has arrived.
